uncited: It sets itself apart by integrating real-time geometric modification (sculpting) directly into the rendering pipeline via GPU-based distance lookups, building on the [GPU-based Volume Sculpting System](13711-gpu-based-volume-sculpting-system.md) which provides the mechanism for generating the 3D mask.

*   **Input:** A `ClippedImage` containing slices generated by a clipping algorithm; a `SculptBuffer` (3D texture) storing distances to the SRP; transfer functions for shading; a `radius-of-interest` threshold.
It stores distance values to the SRP or modified boundary.
**Maintain 3D Position:** For each fragment, maintain the 3D position of the point that generated it.
*   **Radius-of-interest:** A threshold distance value used in the fragment program to discard fragments.
Typical values are not specified in the sources.
*   **Data Transfer:** The method relies on sending the `SculptBuffer` data back to the GPU as a 3D texture.

*   **Time:** On a PC Pentium 4 (2 GHz, 512 MB RAM) with an ATI 9800 graphics board, rendering a 512x512 image from a VOI of size 512x512x100 took approximately 2.18 msec/image (458 images/sec) for simple GPU rendering.
